title: Paloma and the Spire
premise: Emrys Ashgrove has spent their whole life in Hollowmere, a valley warded against magic, hiding the beast-speech that would mark them for death beyond its borders. When the wards collapse and the stars vanish from the sky, Emrys flees into a world where an ancient entity called the Pale Choir has hollowed out King Aldric and is unmaking the heavens to feed. Guided by a disgraced royal cartographer and a crow who may be more than a crow, Emrys learns their gift was never a curse but a key: only a beast-speaker can hear what remains of the king's true voice inside his stolen body. At the Spire, Emrys must choose between destroying the king to end the Choir or risking everything to free him, discovering that survival bought with silence was never living at all.
about_author: A. M. Galloway is the pen name of a former wildlife rehabilitator who spent a decade listening to animals before writing about them. They live at the edge of a forest, where they insist the crows gossip about them.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. We meet Hollowmere's quiet rhythms and Emrys's secret conversations with animals, including a sharp-tongued crow named Sable. The emotional beat is restless contentment—Emrys loves home but feels caged by the silence they must keep.

chapters.title: Wards Like Old Bones
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The valley's elder reveals the border wards are failing, older than anyone remembers, and no one alive knows how they were made. Emrys hides a flicker of hope that leaving might be possible. Beat: dread mixed with forbidden longing.

chapters.title: The Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. On midwinter night the wards shatter and every star goes dark at once; the animals scream in a language Emrys alone understands. Their mother urges them to stay hidden; instead Emrys packs a bag. Beat: terror crystallizing into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Crows Carried Out
chapters.summary: Sable's POV (rendered through Emrys's gift). Sable recounts fleeing the capital, where the king burned the star-charts and smiled with too many teeth. Beat: horror delivered secondhand, raising stakes beyond the valley.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Debt
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. In the border town of Fenwick, Emrys meets Wren Calloway, a disgraced royal cartographer drunk on failure, who recognizes Emrys's gift when they calm a panicked mule. She offers passage in exchange for help reaching the capital. Beat: wary alliance.

chapters.title: Roads Where Magic Follows
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Outside the valley, ambient magic presses on Emrys like deep water, amplifying their gift until they hear the land itself grieving. Wren teaches them to shield. Beat: overwhelming exposure—the world is louder than Emrys ever feared.

chapters.title: The Choir on the Wind
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. At a refugee camp, survivors describe hearing beautiful singing before loved ones went vacant-eyed and obedient. Emrys realizes the beast-speech and the Choir share a root language. Beat: the personal becomes cosmic.

chapters.title: A King's Empty Eyes
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Flashback chapter: Wren served at court and watched King Aldric change after a night in the old Spire—brilliant, then wrong. Her maps were confiscated; her mentor vanished. Beat: guilt as engine, establishing Wren's debt.

chapters.title: Teeth in the Tall Grass
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A Choir-hound ambushes the party; Emrys speaks to it and discovers the hounds are made from taken people, still screaming inside. They kill it, and Emrys vomits. Beat: first blood, and the cost of knowing your enemy.

chapters.title: The City of Borrowed Light
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The capital survives under lamplight and denial; posters promise the stars will return if citizens report 'the gifted.' Emrys must pass as ordinary while beasts whisper warnings everywhere. Beat: paranoia and claustrophobia.

chapters.title: Old Friends, New Prices
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren seeks her old contact, spymaster Odile, who agrees to help—but demands Emrys be handed over to the Crown if the mission fails. Wren signs anyway. Beat: loyalty purchased with betrayal in reserve.

chapters.title: Beneath the Chapel Floor
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. In the palace crypts, Emrys finds pre-Choir carvings showing beast-speakers binding the Spire long ago—they were wardens, not witches. Beat: identity reframed; the gift has a purpose and a history.

chapters.title: The Voice Inside the Crown
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. During a forced audience, Emrys hears beneath the king's ringing decrees a faint, drowning human voice begging for help. It is Aldric, still alive in there. Beat: hope that complicates everything—killing him is no longer simple.

chapters.title: Sable's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable confesses she once served the Choir as a spy and led it to Hollowmere's edge years ago; her loyalty since has been penance. Emrys, furious, nearly casts her out. Beat: trust shattered and painfully renegotiated.

chapters.title: The Unbinding Rite
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Odile's scholars assemble fragments of the old rite: a beast-speaker can sever the Choir from the king, but the speaker risks being pulled into the Choir's song permanently. Emrys volunteers; Wren refuses to allow it. Beat: love versus sacrifice.

chapters.title: What Stays Invisible
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. On the eve of the attempt, Emrys confronts their lifelong strategy of hiding: invisibility kept them safe and useless. They write a letter to their mother they may never send. Beat: quiet reckoning with self before the storm.

chapters.title: Ascension
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The party infiltrates the Spire during the king's star-unmaking ritual. Wren holds the door; Sable flies interference; Emrys climbs toward the crown. Beat: breathless ascent, allies spending themselves to buy one chance.

chapters.title: The Song That Eats Names
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Face to face with the Choir wearing Aldric, Emrys is drawn into its song, which offers them belonging, power, an end to loneliness. They nearly dissolve—until they hear the king's true voice singing their name back. Beat: climax of temptation and identity.

chapters.title: Two Voices, One Throat
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Instead of fighting the Choir alone, Emrys harmonizes with Aldric's trapped will, using the rite to tear the entity loose. The king collapses, freed but broken; the Choir retreats into the Spire's foundations, wounded. Beat: costly victory.

chapters.title: The Price of the Key
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The rite has left part of the Choir's song lodged in Emrys's mind—a cold chorus they must learn to silence daily. Wren tends them; Sable keeps watch. Beat: survival achieved, but changed; the theme's price made flesh.

chapters.title: Stars, Relit
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV shifts. With the king restored, the great wardens' network is rebuilt; the first new star kindles over the capital. Aldric publicly honors beast-speakers, ending the persecution. Beat: catharsis, public restoration of what was hidden.

chapters.title: Home, Louder Than Before
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys returns to Hollowmere—not to hide, but to teach other gifted children what their voices are for, with Wren mapping the way and Sable riding their shoulder. Beat: resolution—identity chosen, loyalty earned, survival transformed into living.
